title: Actinomyces Infection in Pregnancy: A Rare and Silent Cause of Preterm Delivery – Case Report and Literature Review
content: Intrauterine infection in pregnancy leading to inflammation of the foetal membranes – chorion and amnion (chorioamnionitis) is a leading cause of preterm birth (PTB). It is thought that this process begins with bacterial invasion of the amniotic fluid with progression to involvement of the membrane and possibly choriodecidua. Causative organisms implicated aside from bacteria include viral and fungal pathogens. Amongst the reported bacterial causes of Chorioamnionitis, Actinomyces spp has been rarely reported as a causative agent. Infection with Actinomyces in pregnancy has been noted to result in a high incidence of preterm delivery.  It is therefore important that the placenta from preterm delivery is appropriately examined through microbiologic methods and should also be sent for histopathologic examination. Where chorioamnionitis is identified on histopathologic examination, a careful search for the offending organisms should be undertaken.  This ensures that an appropriate antibiotic management regime is recommended for the baby and mother.
